ashby:artificialanalysis:c5437ebc-ae37-4.summary:
Artificial Analysis is the leading independent AI benchmarking company. We support labs, engineers and enterprises to understand AI capabilities and make critical decisions about their AI strategies. We are the go-to authority for understanding AI, from AI labs and enterprises to media, investors, and policymakers. Our benchmarks don’t just measure the cutting edge of AI, they are actively shaping the frontier.

Our benchmarks and analysis are trusted by hundreds of thousands of users and are the go-to reference for leading AI labs including OpenAI, Google, Meta, NVIDIA and Anthropic, and major publications including the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, the Financial Times and The Economist.

sections.title: About Artificial Analysis
paras: We are a team of 40+, on track to double by end of year, backed by Nat Friedman (GitHub, Meta), Daniel Gross (SSI, Meta), Andrew Ng (Google Brain, DeepLearning.ai , Amazon), Adam D’Angelo (Quora, Poe, OpenAI), Clem Delangue (Hugging Face) and other industry leaders.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Speech is becoming AI’s next interface: text to speech, speech to text, voice cloning and real-time voice agents are moving from demos into infrastructure, and our speech benchmarks are how the industry tracks who is winning. We’re hiring into our speech pillar to drive that coverage.

You’ll build and extend our speech evaluations and arenas, from streaming speech to text and voice cloning to next-generation speech-to-speech intelligence with benchmarks like AgentTalk, and work at a deep technical level with the leading speech AI companies to benchmark their latest models as they launch.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
paras: • Benchmark the Speech Frontier: Own coverage across text to speech, speech to text and speech to speech, benchmarking new models and providers as they launch

• Design Speech Evaluations: Build and extend the evaluation frameworks, prompt libraries and arenas that reflect how developers and creators actually use speech models, including agentic voice through AgentTalk
• Partner with Speech Leaders: Work with the top speech AI companies in the world at a deep technical level to benchmark their models and shape how the industry measures voice

sections.title: What We’re Looking For
paras: You should know speech AI from the inside.

Backgrounds include: product, research or engineering roles at speech AI companies (e.g. ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Inworld, Sesame, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Rime or similar), voice teams at larger platforms (e.g. OpenAI, Google, Microsoft), or teams building products on text to speech, speech to text or real-time voice.

ashby:ashby:dfc35159-ffe5-4d42-bea3-552b.summary:
As the Enterprise Solutions Engineering Manager at Ashby, you’ll lead and grow a high-performing team of Solutions Engineers who own our most strategic, complex deals. Your team partners closely with Enterprise Account Executives to secure both the technical and commercial win—guiding large organizations through deep technical evaluations and showing them how Ashby can fundamentally transform the way they hire.

You’ll be responsible for shaping and scaling the enterprise SE motion at Ashby: hiring exceptional talent, coaching them toward mastery, operationalizing excellence, and refining the processes that help the team—and the business—win more often and more efficiently.

sections.title: Product-Market Fit That Makes Your Team’s Job Easier
paras: Your team will support a product that prospects genuinely love—and often ask to buy before the demo ends. This creates a coaching environment focused on technical excellence and deal strategy, not convincing skeptics.

sections.title: Product Depth That Rewards Real Solutioning
paras: Ashby is a deeply configurable product, and enterprise prospects come with highly specific, nuanced hiring processes. Your team won’t be running generic demos—they’ll be diagnosing how each organization hires and architecting solutions that map Ashby’s capabilities to those workflows. The coaching opportunity here is rich: breadth across the full product, depth in custom solutioning, and the creativity to show prospects something they didn’t know was possible.

sections.title: A Leadership Role Designed for Builders
paras: You’ll inherit an enterprise SE motion that works and level it up. The initiatives you lead—from POC frameworks to RFP libraries to competitive playbooks—will define how the enterprise SE team operates for years to come.

sections.title: A Seat at the Product Table
paras: You’ll work in tight collaboration with Product and Engineering, translating enterprise field insights directly into roadmap input. The problems your team uncovers shape what Ashby builds next.

ashby:assorthealth:7009edfe-b57d-43df-94.summary:
Every time you call a doctor's office, the system forgets you the moment you hang up. You wait on hold, explain everything from scratch, get bounced between lines, and hope someone follows up. Everyone has felt this. No one should have to.

At Assort Health, we're building one continuous conversation for every patient. An AI agent that knows who you are, remembers how you like to be reached, and carries that context from your first symptom to your full recovery. What began as the first voice AI agent to schedule a specialty appointment has become the largest proprietary specialty dataset in healthcare: 345 million patient interactions, 62,000 care protocols, 1.6 million decision pathways.

sections.title: Building Healthcare That Remembers
paras: We went from 15 people in 2025 and will cross 250 by the end of 2026. Revenue is up 20x in 15 months and we've raised $222 million, including a recent $120 million Series C at a $1.2 billion valuation from investors including Menlo Ventures and Lightspeed. We've also been named to the Forbes Cloud 100 and the 2026 Enterprise Tech 30 as the only healthcare AI company on the list!
Healthcare spends $1.1 trillion a year on administration instead of care. If you want to help change that, apply below.

sections.title: The Role
paras: Agent Product Management is the fastest growing team at Assort. Agent Product Managers (APMs) design, launch, and tune our AI agents inside real customer practices, and Agent Strategy Managers (ASMs) own strategic, long-term customer relationships. Together they sit between product, implementation, and the customer.

As Director, you will own Assort's largest multi-site and multi-product customers outside of health systems, such as large specialty groups and multi-practice platforms. A single rollout can span many locations and several use cases, including inbound scheduling, outreach, referrals, intake, and payments. These are long-term relationships, so you are accountable for both getting them live and growing them.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Lead and scale the APM and ASM teams serving Enterprise and Strategic accounts, and own the hiring bar, team structure, and career development as the function grows.
Serve as the executive owner for your largest accounts, working directly with customer VP and C-suite stakeholders and leading the hard conversations yourself.
Own the rollout plan for each account: sequencing, capacity, dependencies, and the tradeoffs when a customer wants more than the team can deliver.
Own portfolio performance, including time-to-launch, agent performance, abandonment, hold time, conversion, and staffing capacity, and catch systemic risk before it becomes an escalation.
Step into the most complex deployments and escalations yourself and lead from the front.
Partner with Sales and Customer Success on handoffs, expansion, and renewal risk, and push back when commitments outrun what the team can deliver.
Build the Enterprise playbook: scoping, account planning, executive reporting, and how we expand a customer from one use case to many.
Bring field insight to Product and Engineering, including what strategic customers need that the roadmap doesn't yet cover.

sections.title: What We're Looking For
bullets: 8 to 10 years across consulting, investment banking, or tech (ideally MBB, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Google, Amazon, or Meta), plus experience at a fast-growing tech company or startup.

Operator experience, such as founding a company, running operations, or holding GM or P&L responsibility. We weigh this heavily because the role is closer to running a business than managing a product.
Experience leading complex, multi-workstream enterprise rollouts and digital or AI transformations, including change management.
Executive presence with senior customer and cross-functional stakeholders. You can brief a frustrated executive clearly and lead with the headline.
Proven people leadership. You have hired, developed, and managed teams, and you can describe how you know each week whether your team is on track.
Systems thinking and capacity modeling. You can turn lessons from one account into a reusable playbook and plan team capacity across a portfolio.
Willingness to push back on customers, Sales, and leadership when a commitment isn't realistic, while keeping the relationship strong.
Experience building or implementing AI solutions, or using AI to build agents and systems.

ashby:auror:cf551fbe-f055-45b6-8939-a643.summary:
At Auror, we’re empowering the retail industry to tackle theft and Organised Retail Crime, a $150 Billion problem globally. It’s high volume crime that’s increasingly organised in nature and is putting people, retailers, and communities at risk every day.

Founded in New Zealand 12 years ago, we’re working with some of the best and largest retailers in the world across the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and the UK. Auror is connecting people and intelligence to reduce crime. We’re using technology for good.

Our mission is clear: reduce violent retail crime by 50% in 5 years. It's an ambitious goal - and one we believe is achievable. In partnership with our leading retail partners, we need people with the passion, determination, and innovation required to overcome one of the world's largest problems. If you’re looking to make a difference with and for the people dedicated to…

sections.title: About Auror
paras: We're also embracing the potential of AI to supercharge our impact - whether that's enhancing the way we detect trends, support our customers, or improve internal workflows. As a company, we're committed to responsibly incorporating AI into how we work and what we build, and we encourage all Aurors to be curious about how AI can elevate their work, regardless of role or function.

sections.title: The Role
paras: The role of the Customer Success Manager is to drive long-term strategic value and deep product integration across our enterprise partnerships. Once a customer is activated, you take the lead—owning the ongoing relationship and ensuring our platform becomes an indispensable part of their daily operations and crime reduction strategy. This role reports to the Customer Success Lead.

You are a strategic advisor who understands the "big picture." By analyzing health metrics, running refreshed engagement practices, and developing success plans, you will ensure our customers don't just use the platform, but achieve measurable, high-impact outcomes. You will bridge the gap between software and strategy, turning active users into lifelong champions.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Strategic Account Direction: Own the post-onboarding lifecycle for enterprise-level customers, defining the long-term vision and success roadmap to ensure sustained ROI.
Drive Deep Adoption: Move beyond basic usage to ensure the platform is "embedded" in the customer's culture and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Refreshed Engagement Practices: Lead high-impact business reviews (QBRs/CVRs) and executive briefings that move away from "feature updates" toward "outcome storytelling."
Growth & Expansion: Partner with Retail Partnership Managers & Account Executives to identify opportunities, new department rollouts, and upsell potential based on the customer’s evolving needs.
Outcome Analytics: Transform complex data sets into actionable insights, proving the platform’s value in reducing shrink, improving safety, and optimizing operations.
Champion Development: Cultivate deep relationships with senior loss prevention stakeholders, turning them into vocal advocates for Auror.
Cross-Functional Advocacy: Serve as the "Voice of the Customer" for the Product team, providing feedback that shapes the future of the platform based on mature user needs.
Consultative Change Management: Support customers through organisational shifts, ensuring our technology remains central to their evolving business processes.

sections.title: About You
bullets: The Strategic Partner: You have experience in Enterprise Customer Success or Account Management (SaaS preferred). You know how to navigate complex hierarchies and speak the language of senior leaders.
Data-Driven Storyteller: You don't just report numbers; you explain what they mean. You can take raw engagement data and turn it into a compelling narrative about crime reduction and business value.
Growth Mindset: You have a "commercial eye" and can naturally spot opportunities where our platform can solve additional problems for a customer.
Master of Influence: You excel at driving change without direct authority, coaching customers to adopt new habits and "better ways of working."
Proactive Problem Solver: You don't wait for a customer to flag an issue. You monitor health metrics and intervene early to course-correct engagement before it dips.
Collaborative & Adaptive: You enjoy working in a specialised ecosystem, seamlessly taking over the "baton" from the Activation team to lead the long-term marathon.
Mobile & Connected: You are comfortable with regular travel to build face-to-face rapport and attend industry events.

ashby:avoca:335a39ed-93b8-467f-8b4e-543e.summary:
Avoca is transforming how home service companies engage with their customers. Our AI-powered conversational agents handle every high-value inbound call, from booking jobs, qualifying leads, and driving higher revenue, all at a speed and consistency unmatched by human call centers.

We're a Series B startup backed by Kleiner Perkins, Meritech Capital, General Catalyst, and other top-tier investors, with $125M raised and a $1B valuation. We grew 10x in 2025 and have scaled to 170+ employees in under two years across our NYC headquarters and Santa Barbara office.

In a $1T+ market where 85% of missed calls go to competitors, we're building the category-defining platform for AI-driven customer engagement, serving the largest brands in home services. With high-energy, in-office teams in both locations, every hire here has an immediate and visible impact.

paras: We're hiring a Channel Partner Manager to build one of Avoca's most important revenue engines: partnerships with the HVAC manufacturers, OEMs, and distributors that sit upstream of every contractor. Avoca has established itself as the leading brand and AI partner in the home services industry through partnerships across several channels, and this role owns distribution through the OEM and supplier layer. bullets: Own a portfolio of partner relationships end to end, from first conversation to signed partnership to revenue
Build partnerships across HVAC manufacturers, OEMs, distributors, and their territory managers, including the co-op programs that fund and shape how these partnerships work
Structure partnerships that create real distribution: co-marketing, referral motions, preferred-vendor positioning, joint events, and go-to-market
Turn relationships into measurable partner-sourced pipeline and ARR, and own those numbers
Represent Avoca with partners and at industry events, with travel as needed, heavier during conference season
Work closely with Sales, RevOps, and Marketing to convert partner introductions into closed business

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL BRING
bullets: Direct experience in the home services industry building channel partnerships with HVAC manufacturers and distributors like Trane, Daikin, Carrier, or Ferguson
Existing relationships you can activate quickly, with manufacturer channel leaders and distributor territory managers, plus an understanding of how co-op works
Experience with channel, co-marketing, or partner-sourced revenue motions
4+ years of professional experience, with 6 to 10 years the ideal range
A track record of building and closing partnerships or commercial relationships, not just managing existing ones
Strong commercial instinct and clear communication with both field operators and executives
High agency and pace: you build the playbook and move at the speed of a high-growth startup, not a legacy player

sections.title: WHO YOU ARE
bullets: You know the home services world well enough to bring a point of view and a network with you, not build both from scratch
You're a relationship builder who's equally comfortable in the field and in a boardroom
You think in systems: you can look at a fragmented landscape and quickly see where the leverage is
You want to own a book of partnerships, carry a number, and shape what this function becomes

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:

Develop buyer personas and deepen our understanding of customer needs, pain points, and purchasing decisions.

Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Solutions to influence product strategy and roadmap priorities based on customer and market feedback.

sections.title: Who You Are:
paras: You’re a builder and operator who thrives in fast-moving, high-accountability environments. You take pride in getting things done — thoughtfully, efficiently. You’re energized by ambiguity, skilled at bringing clarity, and comfortable flexing between strategy and execution. You value feedback — giving it, receiving it, and acting on it — and you see collaboration as a competitive advantage, not a burden. You’re low-ego but high-agency: you care about winning as a team more than being right individually. You move quickly, communicate directly, and make decisions grounded in impact and data.
You don’t need constant direction — you create momentum. You take ownership for outcomes, and you expect the same from those around you.

ashby:babbel:a434532f-87f2-49f7-84e1-d1e.summary: Are you passionate about learning languages? About helping people connect and communicate across cultures, for travel, friendship, or career advancement? About making an impact to our company and our 25MM+ learners? Come join our NY-based team as a Product Manager, Marketing Tech

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: We are looking for a Product Manager, Marketing Tech to help Babbel’s marketing teams reach learners with reliable, privacy-conscious marketing technology. Working closely with the Growth Product Director and Engineering Manager, you’ll own the roadmap for the MarTech team and enable a global team of marketers to grow Babbel’s subscription base.

The MarTech team maintains and improves Babbel’s marketing tech stack. It enables marketing teams to integrate with partner solutions and to launch, manage, and optimize campaigns efficiently, while ensuring data fidelity and compliance. The team also bridges our offices in Berlin and New York and the departments that depend on marketing data. You’ll be the product lead for an agile, cross-functional team and work day to day with Engineering, Data & Analytics, Marketing, Legal and Privacy, and external partners, from discovery through delivery and measurement.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Set direction and priorities: Own the marketing technology roadmap, aligned to company strategy and OKRs. Run end-to-end product development and make trade-offs clear across user needs, business value, effort, and risk.

Improve tracking and measurement: Guide web and app tracking, including event definitions, session logic, data enrichment, and attribution, across client-side, server-side, and server-to-server setups. Partner with Engineering and Analytics to keep data accurate and useful for marketing decisions.
Embrace AI-assisted development: Work with fast-moving engineers. Use AI tools to write and refine features and user stories, and build AI prototypes to test ideas early.

Develop audience and activation capabilities: Shape how consented customer data flows across channels through Tealium CDP. With Marketing, Data, and Engineering, define use cases, data needs, identity and consent rules, integrations, and success measures.

Support partner measurement: Improve Adjust integrations for mobile attribution and partner performance. Coordinate conversion events, postbacks, API changes, and data-quality checks with internal and external partners.

Own consent and privacy tooling: Manage OneTrust product needs, including consent experiences, configuration, testing, and SDK and event alignment, to support GDPR, CCPA, and other requirements. Work with Legal and Privacy on interpretation and implementation.

Run effective discovery and delivery: Work closely with marketers to understand their needs, define problems and requirements, and write concise documentation. Take work from hypothesis and MVP through launch, monitoring, and iteration.
Measure outcomes: Set hypotheses and success metrics before delivery. Use experiments, dashboards, and user feedback to evaluate and improve features.

sections.title: Tools & Systems
bullets: Core: OneTrust, Adjust, Tealium, Google Tag Manager, web and mobile tracking SDKs, partner APIs and conversion events, and payment integrations such as Stripe.
Analytics and experimentation: Google Analytics 4, Amplitude, Tableau, StatSig, and proprietary tools.
Data: SQL-based warehouses such as DataBricks.

sections.title: What you bring
bullets: 3+ years of experience in product management, ideally working with backend engineers.
Experience implementing ad tracking for websites and apps, and integrating third-party services via client-side, server-to-server, and via API connections.
In-depth knowledge of client-side and server-side marketing tracking with tag management tools (Google Tag Manager and Tealium).
Hands-on experience with consent and privacy management systems such as OneTrust, and a working understanding of GDPR and CCPA.
A good understanding of marketing and online user behavioral analysis.
Strong analytical skills: you enjoy working with data and pay attention to detail.
Clear communication and proactive stakeholder management across marketers, engineers, legal partners, and external vendors.
Strong project and time management, with the ability to juggle multiple stakeholders, priorities, and contexts in parallel.

ashby:code-metal:b110301c-5000-4752-bfc8.summary: Code Metal is the leader in automated software engineering you can trust. As AI writes more of the world's code, the bottleneck in software has shifted from writing code to verifying it works, and AI cannot verify its own work with certainty. Code Metal takes a fundamentally different approach: constrain AI to what it does reliably, verify every step independently of the model using formal methods, and keep engineers in the loop on the decisions that matter. The result isn't code that probably works — it's code that is provably correct, with auditable proof. Customers including the U.S. Air Force, L3Harris, RTX, and Toshiba use Code Metal to modernize legacy code, optimize performance on real hardware, and move prototypes to production, fast. Founded in 2023 with offices in Boston and San Francisco, Code Metal is funded by Accel, Salesforce Ventures, B Capital, Smith Point Capital, J2…

sections.title: Role Overview
paras: We're seeking a senior product leader to own Cohere's Inference as a Service business end to end. The product is sovereign, self-serve inference: a mid-market or enterprise buyer picks a model, a region and a GPU size, and is running the same afternoon with no procurement cycle and no infrastructure of their own. You'll decide which open-weights and first-party models we serve, in which regions and on which hardware, set the rate card they sell at, and carry the revenue and margin that follow from those calls. You own the platform around that endpoint as well, from the console and dashboards a customer administers their deployment through to the catalog of first-party and third-party models behind it.

You'll set the strategy and run the execution, which means choosing where to spend across serving efficiency, the self-serve console and regional capacity when all three want the same budget, and shipping the deployment framework that removes infrastructure barriers while holding the line on data residency, compliance and operational confidence. You'll do that across engineering, serving, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority over most of it, and you'll be accountable for the outcome rather than for the roadmap.

The timing is most of the opportunity. Every serious company is deciding where its models will run and what it costs to keep them running, serving demand is climbing faster than anyone can rack hardware for it, and very few of those buyers are willing to hand their data to an operator who can read it. We are starting this business from a standing start, with the models, the silicon and the encryption already in place and almost no one else able to offer the combination. You would be taking a product to market in the window where that advantage is still ours, building one of Cohere's major revenue lines from its first customer onward, and shaping how a generation of companies buys AI it can actually trust.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Own the P&L for Inference as a Service: carry the revenue number, set the rate card, and keep blended margin above the floor as the catalog and the fleet grow.

Own the inference platform itself: the console and dashboards where customers see usage, spend, API keys, access control and attestation, and the value-add tooling that makes a managed endpoint worth more than a raw one.

Own the model inventory across first-party and third-party models: what enters the catalog, how it is grouped by provenance, what it is priced at, and when something is quantised, replaced or retired.
Set the roadmap and the investment case across serving efficiency, the self-serve surface and regional capacity, and make the call when those three compete for the same budget.

Build the commercial motion with GTM from the ground up: self-serve acquisition for the mid-market, a sales-led motion for enterprise, and the partnerships that monetise capacity we would otherwise leave idle.

Stay close to the market: talk to customers and developers about integration friction and unmet needs, track competitor pricing, catalogs and launches, and follow where models and hardware are heading, then turn that into a clear view of where we should place our bets and what it would take to win.
Define the metrics that tell us whether this is a business, including revenue, margin, win rate, time to first token and self-serve share, and lead the work that moves them.
Partner with engineering, research, legal, finance, technical writing and developer relations to ship the platform and clear the licensing, pricing and capacity decisions behind it.

sections.title: Requirements
bullets: 10+ years of product management experience, including meaningful time owning a B2B infrastructure or platform product at the scope of a business rather than a feature area.
Experience operating in a GM-like capacity: you have carried a revenue line or a P&L, set pricing, and been held to margin as well as to shipping.

Background at a neocloud such as Together AI, Baseten or Fireworks, or at a hyperscaler such as AWS, Azure, OCI or Google Cloud, with a working view of how inference capacity is priced, packaged and sold, and a point of view on where the segment goes next.
A track record of thinking about infrastructure as a product, with the ability to translate system-level capabilities into clearly differentiated, customer-facing features.
Entrepreneurial, with experience taking a new product to market and building the commercial motion around it rather than inheriting one.

Experience with deployment models such as multi-tenant and dedicated infrastructure, and ownership across the full product lifecycle, from problem definition through launch, iteration and eventual migration or deprecation.
Analytical by default: you define success metrics before you build, instrument thoughtfully, and use data alongside qualitative feedback to make decisions.

Able to set direction and earn alignment across engineering, infrastructure, finance, legal and GTM without formal authority, and to put a clear recommendation and its trade-offs in front of an executive audience.

PHIL is a Series D health-tech company building the platform that connects patients, prescribers, pharmacies, and pharmaceutical manufacturers so patients can get their medication quickly and affordably.

Our digital hub and pharmacy platform handles everything from enrollment and benefits verification to prior authorization, copay support, and home delivery. For manufacturers, that means more patients start therapy and stay on it, plus the commercial insight to keep improving access.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're hiring a Senior Director of Product, Coverage to own coverage at PHIL end to end: the coverage engine (real-time benefit verification, prior authorization, and plan-specific appeals) and the product foundation it runs on, including the EHR, payer, and partner integrations that make it work. This is a general manager role with full ownership of outcomes and the freedom to pivot as we learn. It is not a project management or delivery-coordination role.

You'll decide what we build, what we buy, and which partners we connect to, always in service of one question: how many more patients get covered and start therapy, and how quickly. Coverage determines how fast we can bring on new therapies and how well we serve patients, so this role is central to PHIL's growth and launch success right now.

You'll report to the Vice President of Product Management and work closely with Business Development, Engineering, Design, and Pharmacy Operations. You'll lead strategy, requirements, and prioritization, while those teams bring the partner relationships, technical build, user experience, and operational expertise.

sections.title: What you'll own
bullets: Business outcomes: Own the business outcomes of coverage, not just the features. That means (1) growth and coverage performance, (2) new capabilities, and (3) expansion into new therapeutic areas. You own delivery and success: not only what gets built, but how it works in the real world and whether it moves the numbers.
Business strategy: Be a strategic partner who informs and molds PHIL's business strategy. You push back when needed, bring solutions rather than just problems, and help the business focus.

Coverage strategy and roadmap: Own the end-to-end roadmap for coverage: benefit verification, prior authorization, and appeals. Tie it to PHIL's business strategy and to measurable patient-start outcomes.

The coverage funnel: Understand every step from prescription to approved therapy start, find where patients and prescribers drop out, and prioritize the highest-leverage fixes rather than relying on averages.

Prescriber (HCP) experience: Make coverage tasks happen where prescribers already work, through the EHR, minimizing HCP effort and friction. Be rigorous about how prescribers really behave today and why they would choose our workflow over alternatives.

Integrations and product foundation: Own the roadmap for external integrations (EHRs, payers and plans, third-party providers) and the platform capabilities beneath them, with a clear point of view on build vs. buy, with speed and quality as the test.

Competitive and partner landscape: Maintain an honest view of the competitive landscape and PHIL's strengths and gaps, with a plan to close them. Manage partnerships to secure the right level of access and execution, and drive a well-executed payer and network adoption plan.
Metrics and operational KPIs: Set long-term success metrics, KPIs, and SLAs for coverage and integrations, and report on them to leadership.

sections.title: What success looks like in your first year
bullets: By 90 days: You've mapped the coverage funnel and our current coverage landscape, met key partners and internal stakeholders, and identified the biggest leaks and opportunities, backed by data. You've performed a product-level competitive benchmarking analysis and shared an initial assessment with senior leadership.

By 6 months: You've delivered a prioritized coverage and integrations roadmap with defined KPIs and agreed build-vs-buy decisions, and shipped at least one quick win that measurably improves benefit verification or prior authorization speed or quality.

By 12 months: At least one new integration capability is live that drives speed or a positive improvement in coverage, and it is hitting its targets, including measurable reduction in HCP effort. Coverage KPIs and SLAs are tracked and reported to leadership, and the roadmap is supporting at least one new therapeutic category.

sections.title: About the role:
paras: Skydio runs its business on Palantir Foundry. Sales, finance, manufacturing, and operations teams build the apps they work in every day there, and some of that data reaches our customers directly in our products. Underneath all of it is one ontology: the shared business objects, actions, and links that connect our systems - that people and AI agents use to find and act on company data. New use cases for work in Foundry are growing fast, and each one should land on that shared model rather than beside it.

Our Business Data Platform team is hiring a data product manager to help own that ontology and the path from a team's idea to a working use case. You will learn how each part of the business operates, decide what to reuse, extend, or build, and keep the model clean as it grows. You will work closely with our data security engineer so new use cases land in the right place with the right protections. You will report to the head of Business Data Platform.

sections.title: How you'll make an impact:
bullets: Own and evolve the Foundry Ontology with the head of Business Data Platform: the stable business objects, actions, and links between them (accounts, orders, sites, parts, people) that every app and agent builds on, designed so new use cases plug in without rework
Learn how our GTM, finance, manufacturing, and operations teams run, and model it so data from Salesforce, NetSuite, Workday, and our other systems connects in one place

Work with leaders to decide what the business needs to see now, and turn it into metrics, dashboards, and apps on the ontology, knowing when to build around imperfect data and when to push for a fix at the source

Run intake for new use cases: help each team define its objects, actions, and who can see and do what, then decide what to reuse, extend, or build, and who builds it, including our Palantir forward deployed engineers
Work with our data security engineer to place each new use case in the right project and access boundary, so teams can build quickly on protected data

Keep the ontology clean and well typed, with clear names, descriptions, and types, so people and AI agents can find the right object and use it correctly. Bring these standards to our cross-functional Data Council
Connect systems through the ontology and its APIs, so internal apps, integrations, and some customer-facing products read and write the same governed data

We started Timely to build the tool we wish we had when we were in schools. And today, we are changing how schools create high quality schedules for teachers and students. Timely combines groundbreaking AI technology with support from a team of expert school schedulers: saving schedulers’ time, and surfacing opportunities for leaders to unlock staff potential. sections.title: Who we are

sections.title: About the Role
paras: This role is for an experienced product manager who is comfortable operating at the intersection of “hard” algorithmic systems and “soft” customer problems. You'll work together on a product squad with the engineers who build and tune the optimizer. You will own the strategy that brings users from their constraints to optimized schedules, defining the optimization process and experience, validating improvements with customers, and using a blend of AI and UI to ensure the complexity of problem-solving is expressed as simply as possible.

This role will balance technical collaboration with product judgment - deciding which optimizer enhancements are worth pursuing, how to measure their effectiveness, and how to design the surrounding experience so that schedulers understand what the optimizer is doing and why. You'll ensure product decisions are clear, priorities are well-communicated, and our roadmap reflects the diverse needs of school schedulers and the demanding needs of a fast-growing business..

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Engage with customers to understand opportunities to generate better K12 school schedules.
Dive deep enough into the optimizer technology and scheduling domain to facilitate critical decisions with our engineering team. Drive those decisions forward with accountability.
Partner with Engineering to surface and refine improvements to the optimizer’s core algorithms, model-builders, and orchestration pipeline to meet user needs.

Collaborate with engineering to design and execute experiments that test optimizer changes, defining consistent performance and quality metrics (e.g., feasibility rate, schedule quality scores, solve time, constraint violations) that determine whether an enhancement is actually working.

Craft optimizer product requirements: defining and refining new product features that are built on (and inspire) new computational capabilities. Work with engineering (and AI agents) to break down requirements into well-defined stories.
Leverage AI to knit together requirements, story definition, and development workflows.
Develop and implement a vision for how generative AI can improve algorithmic optimization of schedules.

Own the end-to-end experience of how school schedulers interact with the optimizer — including how results, tradeoffs, and edge cases like infeasible or sub-optimal solutions are communicated and resolved.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: TLS is the connective tissue of the Internet, and Cloudflare terminates a large fraction of it. Cloudflare sits in front of more than 20 percent of global Internet request traffic and terminates TLS for millions of domains. Every day, our network handles certificate operations across products like Universal SSL, SSL for SaaS, Origin CA, Cloudflare Access, and Cloudflare Tunnel.

That scale has taught us how the WebPKI ecosystem works from the consuming side. As certificate lifetimes shorten, agentic activity increases, and post-quantum certificates move toward production, the number of certificates the Internet depends on will grow dramatically.

Cloudflare is building a certificate authority for the whole Internet: a public, redundant, transparent CA that provides another trusted source of automated certificates and helps make the encrypted web more resilient. We intend to be ACME-first, automation-first, and transparent by design. We also intend to lead where the ecosystem is going, including post-quantum certificates and Merkle Tree Certificates, while continuing to support the classic WebPKI customers rely on today.

sections.title: Responsibilities
bullets: Define the product strategy for Cloudflare's CA business across publicly trusted certificates, certificate lifecycle automation, ACME issuance, renewal workflows, revocation, Certificate Transparency, customer controls, developer experience, and integrations with Cloudflare's broader platform.

Build for the whole Internet by understanding the needs of developers, site owners, platform teams, SaaS providers, enterprise security teams, infrastructure operators, and partners who depend on certificates for availability, security, and compliance.

Make resilience a product principle. Help design product requirements that fail small, reduce customer blast radius, support automated recovery, and make certificate replacement fast enough to handle compliance issues, revocation events, or ecosystem incidents.
Drive an ACME-first customer experience that makes it easy for users of existing free or automated CAs to adopt Cloudflare with minimal tooling changes.

Partner closely with engineering on systems that manage certificate lifecycles, automate issuance and renewal, integrate with HSMs, protect keys, support auditability, and operate within strict reliability and correctness requirements.

Partner with compliance, legal, security, and operations to ensure product decisions align with CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, WebTrust audits, root store program policies, Certificate Policy and Certification Practice Statement commitments, and public incident response expectations.
Own go-to-market strategy including packaging, pricing, launch sequencing, competitive positioning, customer segmentation, sales enablement, developer messaging, and adoption metrics.

sections.title: THE POSITION
paras: If this describes you, read on – we want to hear from you!

THE GAME PLAN
Everyone on our team has a part to play
bullets: Drive the integration of our agent layer into the data engineering SDLC: requests arriving from Slack, Jira, GitHub, and PagerDuty, routed into a planning phase that produces scoped, reviewable tickets and a build phase that carries each ticket through spec, plan, build, test, PR, and documentation.
Build the environment that makes agentic engineering actually work: skills, specs, context scaffolding, shared memory, and progressive disclosure.
Extend governed, audited data access so agents operate under each user’s own permissions against our data platform, with a limited blast radius by design.
Define the outer loop: continual learning, post-run review, and agent self-improvement that lands as reviewable pull requests rather than uncontrolled drift.
Advance our strategy-optimization engine from proof of concept to a capability product teams request by name, and land it against real business metrics.

Partner with product to turn ambiguous business problems into optimizable ones: define the action space, the objective and utility weights that encode the tradeoffs we actually care about, and the guardrails and risk tolerance that keep the search honest.

Own the deterministic scoring backbone: versioned scorers, shared and immutable experiment definitions, blind holdout discipline. Ensure results are comparable, auditable, and cumulative across the team rather than trapped in one person’s working directory.
Expand the engine to new scoring and optimization domains across the business, including generosity and promotional spend, module placement and ranking, and search relevance.

sections.title: THE STATS

Define reusable capabilities for offer decisioning, delivery, matching, measurement, and partner integrations; partner with customer-facing PMs on product definitions and end-to-end outcomes.
Treat Kard’s data and developer platforms as products: understand technical users, expand self-service, reduce friction, and measure business impact, quality, trust, reliability, and speed.

sections.title: Desired Skills
bullets: Experience leading technically complex data, ML, or platform products across multiple teams.
A record of turning data or foundational technology into measurable customer and commercial value.

Working fluency across several relevant domains—including data platforms, quality and governance, ML lifecycles, batch and real-time serving, APIs, cloud infrastructure, and developer platforms—and the ability to go deep without replacing engineering leadership.
Fluency in experimentation and measurement, including A/B testing, lift or incrementality, and partnership with data scientists.
Strong discovery and shaping skills with technical users and business stakeholders, and the ability to validate needs directly with external customers.

Founded in 2000, Kaseya was built by builders - and we're still building. We look for people who create rather than wait, who see a hard problem and lean in, and who treat challenges as raw material. At Kaseya, everyone plays a role in shaping the future of IT: whether you're in…

paras: We're building teams that grow, perform, and make an impact. If you're driven by the itch to make things better - a product, a process, a career - you'll fit right in.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: Kaseya is seeking a strategic, detail-oriented Product Manager to join our Business Information Systems (BIS) team. This individual will drive the vision, roadmap, and execution of enterprise capabilities supporting our Product Business Systems (PBS), with a focus on product configuration, pricing, fulfillment, software provisioning, entitlements, usage, and overage management.

This role will support Kaseya’s current operating environment while helping shape the future-state architecture and processes needed to support continued growth and transformation. PBS capabilities span multiple platforms, including Salesforce, NetSuite, integrations, and Kaseya products such as Kaseya One. As Kaseya evolves its enterprise systems landscape, this individual will help guide the transition toward a scalable architecture anchored by Salesforce Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Oracle ERP, and related applications.

The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of the Lead-to-Cash lifecycle within an enterprise SaaS environment, including product and pricing configuration, bundle management, software license provisioning, entitlement management, and usage-based billing. This person must be comfortable navigating complex integrations, balancing competing priorities, and partnering across business and technical teams to simplify legacy processes, strengthen controls, and deliver scalable solutions.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities
bullets: Product Strategy and Roadmap: Define and manage the product roadmap for Product and Pricing, Fulfillment, and Provisioning capabilities, ensuring alignment with corporate strategy, revenue operations priorities, finance transformation goals, customer experience improvements, and future-state migration objectives.

Product and Pricing Management: Lead capabilities related to product configuration, catalog management, SKU creation, product hierarchies, master data governance, pricing models, discount management, renewal pricing, promotions, and bundle configuration.

Fulfillment and Provisioning: Drive requirements and solutions for automated, manual, and hybrid provisioning models, fulfillment routing, tenant and instance creation, customer-to-tenant mapping, license provisioning, and entitlement lifecycle management.

Lead-to-Cash Lifecycle: Lead requirements definition and solution alignment across the Lead-to-Cash lifecycle, including product and pricing setup, order fulfillment, provisioning, usage capture, overage management, billing, revenue recognition, and reporting.

Product Ownership and Agile Delivery: Own and manage the product backlog, develop clear user stories and acceptance criteria, and lead backlog refinement, sprint planning, discovery sessions, solution reviews, demonstrations, and other Agile ceremonies.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Finance, Billing Operations, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Operations, Product, Engineering, Enterprise Architecture, Security, and IT to gather requirements, prioritize initiatives, resolve issues, and deliver scalable business outcomes.

Business Process Optimization: Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce manual intervention, clarify ownership, improve operational handoffs, strengthen governance, and increase automation across PBS capabilities.

Transformation and Migration Readiness: Balance support for legacy systems with future-state transformation priorities, ensuring legacy enhancements deliver measurable value, reduce operational risk, or improve migration readiness.

sections.title: Required Qualifications
bullets: 7+ years of experience in product management, product ownership, business systems analysis, CRM systems, revenue operations systems, or enterprise solution delivery.
Proven experience with Lead-to-Cash, Quote-to-Cash, or subscription lifecycle processes within an enterprise SaaS environment.
Strong working knowledge of Salesforce CPQ, Salesforce Revenue Cloud, Revenue Cloud Advanced, or comparable enterprise product configuration and pricing platforms.
Experience with product catalog management, SKU management, pricing configuration, discounting, bundle management, or product master data governance.
Hands-on experience with software license provisioning, entitlement management, or fulfillment workflows, including integrations using platforms such as MuleSoft or Boomi.
Experience with usage-based pricing models, including usage capture, rating, overage management, and associated billing or revenue processes.
Understanding of integrated system flows across sales, order management, billing, accounts receivable, collections, revenue recognition, and reporting.
Demonstrated success managing cross-functional Agile delivery teams and driving complex enterprise initiatives from requirements through implementation.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Our Customer Success Managers and Renewals Specialists do their best work when the plan, data, and rhythm behind them are solid. This role builds and runs all three. You'll own the numbers and mechanics that tell us who covers which customers, how much capacity we have, and how the book is performing, then turn them into reporting our leaders actually use.

You'll sit between CS leadership, Sales Ops, Finance, and Data. Some weeks you'll be modeling territory options before a quarter starts. sections.title: Capacity, coverage, and assignments
bullets: Maintain headcount and capacity models, and keep them current as hiring, attrition, and book growth change the picture.

Keep assignment data clean and consistent across Salesforce, Gainsight, and reporting, so what the field sees matches what leadership sees.
Flag where coverage doesn't match customer value or risk, and recommend how to fix it.

sections.title: Business reviews and performance reporting
bullets: Build and run the data behind weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews (QBR/MBR), delivering inputs on time and with a clear point of view.
Own renewal ops reporting: upcoming renewals, renewal status and activity, at-risk accounts, and retention outcomes. Forecast and pipeline are owned elsewhere; you'll use the same definitions.
Create and maintain CS dashboards and reports that CSMs, managers and LT rely on to run their books.
Help drive and maintain rhythm of business reporting across all CS and Renewals segments

sections.title: Analysis and improvement
bullets: Answer ad hoc questions from leaders with a recommendation, not a spreadsheet dump.
Spot patterns in the data (churn drivers, coverage gaps, capacity strain) and bring them to the team before they're asked for.
Automate recurring pulls and reports, and document the process so it doesn't live in one person's head.
Work with Sales Ops, Finance, and Data teams to make sure definitions and numbers match across the company.

sections.title: About the role
paras: Our high-touch customers are where the relationship, the stakes, and the revenue are biggest. This role makes sure that book is run like a business: clear on who we serve and how, deliberate about the experience we create, and measured on what it delivers.

This is half strategy, half operator. You'll design customer experiences and programs for our highest-value accounts, and you'll build the operating rhythm, metrics, and processes that keep the high-touch team effective as it grows. You'll work directly with CS leadership, CSMs, Sales, Support, Product, and Marketing, and you'll have room to shape how we serve our biggest customers.

sections.title: Shape the high-touch customer experience
bullets: Design and pilot the moments that matter for high-touch customers: onboarding to value, executive engagement, business reviews, renewal and expansion plays.
Define what high-touch should mean: which customers qualify, what they get, and what outcome each touchpoint should create.
Turn customer feedback and data into specific changes to programs, playbooks, and engagement models.
Work with Product, Support, Marketing, and Sales to close gaps that customers feel across teams.

sections.title: Run the high-touch business
bullets: Own the operating model for the high-touch segment: coverage, capacity, cost to serve, and how the model changes as the customer base grows.
Set the metrics that tell us whether it's working, such as adoption, retention, expansion, and customer sentiment, and build the cadence to review them.
Lead the planning cycles for the segment, and make the case for where to invest and where to automate or pool.
Build the playbooks, workflows, and tooling the team uses, and keep them current.

sections.title: Lead projects across teams
bullets: Manage a portfolio of strategic and operational projects from ambiguous idea to launched, measured program.
Translate leadership priorities into plans with clear owners, timelines, and success measures.
Bring structure to cross-functional problems, flag risks early, and drive adoption of new ways of working.
Prepare clear, decision-ready materials for leadership, with a recommendation attached.

bullets: Develop and execute a comprehensive public sector channel strategy covering Federal Civilian, DoD/IC, and SLED segments, with segment-specific go-to-market plans, ARR targets, and pipeline goals aligned to KnowBe4’s overall revenue objectives.

Build and scale a tiered partner ecosystem comprising public sector-specialized VARs, national and boutique Systems Integrators (e.g., Booz Allen Hamilton, Leidos, SAIC, Peraton, ManTech), distributors (e.g., Carahsoft, Immix Group), and MSSPs, ensuring coverage across all major agency verticals.
Drive significant ARR growth through partner-sourced and partner-influenced opportunities; establish quarterly pipeline, bookings, and growth KPIs for each partner tier and segment.
Identify and capture net-new opportunities by monitoring agency IT modernization initiatives, CISA mandates, zero-trust architecture programs, and Congressional cybersecurity funding priorities.

sections.title: Partner Recruitment, Enablement & Management
bullets: Recruit, onboard, and develop strategic channel partners with demonstrated public sector reach and technical competency in cybersecurity, applying rigorous partner profiling and business-case analysis.

Execute regular business reviews (QBRs) with top-tier partners assessing pipeline health, competitive positioning, and enablement gaps; deliver action plans to accelerate revenue.
Cultivate prime/subcontractor teaming arrangements, positioning KnowBe4 as a preferred subcontractor on large SI-led bids and helping partners build compliant teaming agreements.

bullets: Leverage and expand KnowBe4’s presence on key contract vehicles, including GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS), SEWP V, CIO-SP3, NASA SEWP, and NCPA/NASPO state cooperative contracts, to simplify government procurement.
Guide partners through government acquisition processes, including RFP/RFI responses, IDIQ task orders, BPAs, sole-source justifications, and competitive bid strategies.
Monitor federal and SLED budget cycles, appropriations activity, and continuing resolution (CR) impacts; develop strategies to maintain pipeline momentum regardless of fiscal uncertainty.

sections.title: Compliance, Regulatory Alignment & Risk Management
bullets: In coordination with the Legal team, ensure all channel partner activities comply with applicable federal and state regulations, FAR/DFARS requirements, cybersecurity executive orders (EO 14028), ITAR restrictions, and KnowBe4’s internal compliance standards.

Maintain expert-level knowledge of cybersecurity compliance frameworks relevant to government customers, including FedRAMP, FISMA, CMMC (all levels), NIST SP 800-53/800-171, StateRAMP, and CISA Binding Operational Directives.
Collaborate with Legal, Finance, and Compliance teams to vet partner agreements, channel incentive structures, and government contract terms, minimizing organizational risk.

sections.title: About LearnLux
paras: We’re a venture-backed company that has raised a series B and is supported by experienced investors and long-term partners. We’re a growth-focused business building for scale, and we’re excited by the opportunities and challenges that come with that journey.

sections.title: The Role
paras: At LearnLux, you will build a product that changes lives. Our mission is to empower people to take control of their financial future, whether that means getting out of debt, buying their first home, or preparing for retirement.

As a Senior Product Manager, Platform, you’ll own strategy and roadmap across several foundational areas of our enterprise SaaS platform: data, AI, data compliance, global platform strategy, client integrations, and strategic vendor partnerships. You’ll collaborate with stakeholders across the company to proactively identify the highest-leverage problems and opportunities and turn them into clear product priorities.

This is a highly hands-on role for a Product Manager who is comfortable operating in ambiguity and moving between long-term strategy and detailed execution. You’ll analyze data directly, shape requirements, evaluate tradeoffs, work through complex client and regulatory needs, and partner closely with Engineering and Data to drive initiatives from discovery through delivery.

sections.title: What you’ll do

Use Business Intelligence, AI tools, and agentic workflows to investigate data, validate assumptions, uncover opportunities, and inform product decisions.

Own product direction for client and partner integrations, including HRIS and eligibility feeds, data vendors, implementation partners, and integrations between LearnLux and client systems.

Demonstrated ability to use AI tools to conduct analysis, uncover product or data insights, and improve product decision-making.
Ability to contribute to the design and execution of AI evaluations, including test cases, expected behaviors, and criteria for assessing AI output quality.
Experience working in a startup or similarly fast-moving environment where priorities, processes, and requirements are not already well-defined.
Strong strategic and analytical thinking, with the ability to take ambiguous problem spaces and turn customer, business, data, and technical inputs into a clear strategy and path to execution.

sections.title: Job Title: Implementation Manager, Core
paras:
Location : Remote - US Only
Country : United States
Department : Professional Services
Reports To : Director, Professional Services
Position Type : Full-Time
Salary : $100,000

sections.title: Job Summary:
paras: The Core Implementation Manager (Core IM) is the sole owner of a portfolio of roughly 40+ First Due Core implementations, typically multi-module engagements. These standard and moderately complex projects carry real configuration complexity and frequently include CAD integration and historical data migration, requiring disciplined project management, strong customer command, and the ability to direct several internal specialists toward a single go-live date.

The Core IM owns the customer relationship and every project in the portfolio from contract signature through go-live and handoff to Customer Success, and is accountable for planned duration, scope, risk, customer communication, and time to value. This is a fully autonomous role: you are self-directed on all delivery decisions inside the signed SOW and involve leadership only on commercial and relationship exceptions. Core delivery runs on a paired model: the Implementation Manager owns the project, the assigned Implementation Consultant owns module configuration and functional product depth, and Technical Services owns integration and data migration execution.

sections.title: Key Responsibilities:
bullets: Own a full portfolio of roughly 40+ concurrent Core implementations from contract signature through go-live and handoff to Customer Success, consistently holding planned duration below team goal.

Keep Rocketlane, the system of record, current always (plans, timelines, milestones, task status, owners, and dates) so any colleague can open a project and know exactly where it stands. Complete documentation and exit gates on time, not retroactively.

Lead customer kickoffs with command: set clear expectations, correct unrealistic assumptions in the room, and close with an agreed action list, owners, and dates. Adapt the agenda to each agency’s politics and readiness based on Discovery.
Run a progress cadence of at least bi-weekly check-ins on new acquisition projects and monthly on upsells, using each one to find and remove the real blocker rather than read status.

Tailor each plan to the agency’s operational reality, including shift patterns, governance and approval cycles, budget calendars, and go-live blackout windows. Own multi-module sequencing, phasing, and dependency decisions across the platform.

Direct and sequence the work of Implementation Consultants, Technical Services, Integrations, Support, and Product without direct authority, securing commitment on dates. Module configuration is owned by the assigned Implementation Consultant.
Proactively surface product gaps, process gaps, communication silos, and methodology friction to leadership with supporting specifics and a proposed fix, and help own internal improvement efforts.

Demonstrated ownership of project plans, timelines, risk management, escalation recovery, and scope discipline, including change orders, on projects with multiple internal contributors.

Experience with implementation project management tooling.
Proficiency with Microsoft 365, including Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, and Excel.

sections.title: POSITION SUMMARY
paras: The Regional Account Manager, Southeast (RAM) is a key field position and will have the opportunity to run their own business within their assigned region. sections.title: Position overview
paras: Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship.

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

sections.title: How you'll operate
paras: This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.
bullets: You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.

You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.

You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

sections.title: What you'll have done
bullets: 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).

Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.

Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.

Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.

Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.

A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

sections.title: The first 90 days
paras:
Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras:
The Finance ERP Product Manager leads business-side product management for SAP and related ERP capabilities. Reporting to the Manager, Finance Business Innovation Office (BIO), the role brings together Finance functional subject-matter experts to establish a coordinated business perspective on UHN’s SAP environment, make collective recommendations, and prioritize changes and enhancements based on business value, risk, controls, dependencies and user impact.



The role facilitates the Finance SAP user group and serves as a bridge among Finance process owners and users, BIO, Digital, Data & Analytics, project teams, vendors and implementation partners. The Product Manager is accountable for business product direction, governance, roadmap and backlog coordination, requirements facilitation, business validation and value realization. The FInance ERP Product Manager works in partnership with the Digital team, which retains accountability for technical architecture, configuration, integration engineering, deployment, production support and other technical decisions within its mandate.

In addition to ongoing SAP product management, the role contributes to assessments and implementation initiatives that integrate with SAP and may lead or support other priorities across the BIO portfolio. Assignments may evolve in response to Finance priorities, while remaining consistent with the role’s product-management, business-integration and portfolio responsibilities.

The ERP Product Manager is a proactive, collaborative leader who brings structure and direction to complex, cross-functional priorities. The successful candidate combines strategic product thinking with strong Finance business acumen and a high degree of technical curiosity. They are able to develop a strong working understanding of SAP, its configuration and data, and how it integrates with other systems and applications across the Finance landscape. They are comfortable learning how complex systems work, investigating dependencies and translating between business and technical perspectives so they can effectively challenge assumptions, assess impacts and collaborate with Digital and other technical partners. They are skilled at building consensus among stakeholders with different priorities and balancing business value, risk, urgency, controls and operational readiness. This is a unique opportunity to shape the direction of Finance ERP capabilities and improve how Finance teams use SAP to support reliable, efficient and sustainable operations at UHN.

sections.title: Duties
bullets: Establish and Facilitate the Finance SAP user group, including preparing decision materials, structuring discussions, documenting decisions and actions, and supporting transparent, collective prioritization across functional areas.
Develop and maintain a business-led product vision, roadmap and prioritized backlog for SAP and related Finance ERP capabilities.
Coordinate Finance process owners and functional subject-matter experts in defining business problems, requirements, business rules, controls, user needs and acceptance criteria.
Assess enhancement requests using business value, strategic alignment, risk, urgency, control implications, user impact, dependencies, effort and operational readiness.

Represent the Finance business perspective in discussions with Digital, Data & Analytics, vendors, system integrators and other delivery partners, while maintaining clear separation between business and technical accountabilities.

Support assessments and implementation projects involving interfaces or integrations with SAP, including current-state analysis, options assessment, future-state design, requirements, testing and transition planning.
Identify cross-process and cross-application impacts involving workflows, master data, reporting, controls, integrations and downstream operations.

Coordinate Finance participation in solution reviews, end-to-end testing, user acceptance testing, business readiness, go-live activities and post-implementation review; operational Finance retains accountability for business acceptance.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Undergraduate degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Progressive experience in product management, product ownership, business analysis, Finance systems, ERP implementation or enterprise application management.
Demonstrated experience working with SAP or a comparable enterprise ERP environment supporting Finance processes.
Experience facilitating cross-functional governance or user groups and building consensus among stakeholders with different priorities.
Experience developing roadmaps, managing enhancement backlogs, documenting requirements and acceptance criteria, and coordinating business testing and readiness activities.
Understanding of Finance processes, controls, workflows, master data, reporting and integration dependencies.
Ability to work effectively with technical teams and vendors while maintaining clear business ownership and decision rights.
Strong analytical, facilitation, problem-solving, documentation, communication and stakeholder-management skills.
